from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Polarization and Malus's Law", [
            "Light vibrates in a single plane.",
            "Filter blocks other orientations.",
            "Only vertical wave passes through."
        ])
        
        # Colors
        color_1 = "#00BFFF" # DeepSkyBlue
        color_2 = "#FF4500" # OrangeRed
        color_3 = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        
        # Objects
        # [Asset: Polarization_Vector]
        vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=color_1, buff=0)
        self.place_at_grid(vec, 'B3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # [Asset: Wave_Passing]
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3*x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=color_2)
        self.place_in_area(wave, 'D2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Malus's Law
        equation = MathTex(r"I = I_0 \cos^2(\theta)", color=color_3)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(color_1)
        self.play(Create(vec), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(color_2)
        # Placeholder for filter animation (rotation)
        polarizer = Square(side_length=2, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(polarizer, 'B3', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Rotate(polarizer, angle=PI/4), run_time=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(color_3)
        self.play(Write(equation), run_time=1)
        self.play(Indicate(equation), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = [
            "Combined polarizers create color shifts.",
            "Layers twist polarization angles.",
            "Different wavelengths rotate at different rates.",
            "Observed light shows shifting patterns.",
            "Light intensity creates Barber Pole effect."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Barber Pole Effect Mechanism", lines)
        
        # Create objects for animation
        cylinder = Cylinder(radius=1.0, height=3.0, color="#00CCFF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        stripes = VGroup(*[Line(start=cylinder.get_bottom(), end=cylinder.get_top(), color=WHITE) for _ in range(8)])
        stripes.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeIn(cylinder))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.place_at_grid(cylinder, "C3", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Rotate(cylinder, angle=PI/4, axis=UP))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#1E90FF"))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Formula relates rotation to concentration.",
            "Plot shows rotation versus length.",
            "Slider visualizes changing concentrations.",
            "Vector rotates in real-time.",
            "Colors shift as concentration changes."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Math-Visual Interface", lecture_lines)

        # Formula Setup
        formula = MathTex(r"\theta = [\alpha]lc", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'A2', scale_factor=1.2)

        # Vector Representation
        vector = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(vector, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)

        # Angle Label
        angle_label = MathTex(r"\theta", color=BLUE).next_to(vector.get_tip(), RIGHT)
        self.add(angle_label)

        # Animation logic
        angle = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_vector(mob):
            mob.rotate(angle.get_value() - mob.get_angle())
            
        vector.add_updater(update_vector)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Create(vector))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        slider_bar = Line(self.grid['E2'], self.grid['E5'], color=WHITE)
        slider_knob = Dot(slider_bar.get_start(), color=GREEN)
        self.add(slider_bar, slider_knob)
        self.play(slider_knob.animate.move_to(slider_bar.get_end()))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED)
        self.play(angle.animate.set_value(PI/2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.play(vector.animate.set_color(ORANGE), angle_label.animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Barber Pole Effect: Polarized Light and Chiral Molecules

sections.title: Prerequisite: Polarization and the Malus's Law
sections.content: Define linearly polarized light as an electric field vector vibrating in one plane. Introduce the 'Polarization Filter' as a slit that only allows light in one orientation to pass. Use a 2D animation of a wave passing through a vertical slot to visualize blocking horizontal components.
sections.example: Imagine a picket fence: a rope waving up and down passes through; a rope waving side-to-side is blocked.

sections.title: Introduction to Optical Activity
sections.content: Introduce chiral molecules (sugar). Explain that these molecules act like 'optical prisms' that twist the plane of polarized light as it travels through the solution. This rotation is proportional to the path length and concentration.
sections.example: A hiker walking through a field of 'twisting' tall grass that forces them to tilt their orientation gradually as they move forward.

sections.title: The Barber Pole Effect Mechanism
sections.content: Combine the polarization filter and the sugar solution. As light passes through layers of sugar water, the polarization angle rotates. When placed between two crossed polarizers, different wavelengths (colors) rotate at different rates, creating the 'Barber Pole' color shifting or light intensity modulation.
sections.example: Represent the light vector as a screw thread; as it traverses the syrup, the thread rotates, effectively changing the color observed through the exit polarizer.

sections.title: Visualization: The Math-Visual Interface
sections.content: Present the formula θ = [α]lc. Use a graphical plot where 'θ' (rotation angle) is the Y-axis and 'l' (length) is the X-axis. As a slider moves along the X-axis, show the vector rotating in real-time, matching the degree of rotation to the sugar concentration.
sections.example: A character 'Alice' adjusting a knob (concentration) to see the Barber Pole colors shift from red to blue on a screen.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Saccharimeter
sections.content: Conclude with how this effect is used in the food industry to measure sugar purity. Briefly mention that if the light stops being 'twisted', the sugar might be a racemic mixture or impurities exist.
sections.example: A candy factory quality control sensor using a laser and two polarizers to instantly verify the sweetness level of syrup without touching it.
